tagline.text: A four-story mall near the airport in Lanang, with IMAX and a fountain court

location.label: Location
location.text: J.P. Laurel Avenue, Lanang, Davao City (Brgy. San Antonio, Agdao District)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (especially good as a refuge from midday heat and showers)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (meal, coffee and transport per person, excluding shopping)

children.text: SM Lanang Premier is a large four-story shopping mall in Davao's Lanang district that opened in September 2012, and its official name has been SM Lanang since 2023. It is close to the airport, which makes it easy to visit right after arrival or before departure, and it has an IMAX cinema and a fountain-court dining area.

SM Lanang Premier is a four-story indoor shopping mall on J.P. Laurel Avenue in the Lanang district of Davao City. It is operated by SM Prime Holdings, with construction starting in 2011 and the mall opening on September 28, 2012. SM bought about
10 hectares

of the former Lanang Golf and Country Club grounds to build it, and the building's exterior is said to be inspired by origami. The gross floor area is reported at roughly 133,000 square meters, and the mall had 273 stores when it opened.

It was the 46th SM Supermall to open. From 2011 to 2023 it was called SM Lanang Premier, and in 2023, when SM tidied up the names of its Premier malls, the official name became SM Lanang. Even so, map apps, review sites and local taxi drivers still often say Lanang Premier, so it helps to know both names.
For travelers, the mall's biggest advantage is its location. It is about
2.5km

from Davao International Airport, so it is a short taxi ride from the airport, and it sits at the center of the Lanang district, where hotels and shopping malls cluster. If you have spare time before a flight, you can leave your luggage at your hotel and enjoy a meal and a movie, or you can shop near your accommodation on the evening you arrive. The mall lies between J.P. Laurel Avenue and the S.P. Dakudao loop, so it is easy to reach by car, and it is fairly close to the Davao Museum. Many travelers drop by on the way back to their hotel after sightseeing in the city to wrap up the day.

The anchors are SM Store (department store) and SM Supermarket, and fashion, accessories, appliances, books, restaurants and cafes are spread across the floors. The cinema has six halls plus an IMAX theater, and in May 2026 the IMAX theater finished a refit and reopened with a laser projection system. Behind the mall, the fountain court has restaurants with outdoor seating where you can eat in the cool evening breeze. SM malls are found across the country, so if you are used to traveling in the Philippines the layout and atmosphere will feel familiar. Still, think of it as a base for resting and shopping rather than a main destination when planning your itinerary.

blocks.title: A large mall close to the airport

children.text: At about
2.5km

from Davao International Airport, this is the most convenient large shopping mall to visit right after arrival or before departure. It is a good place to take care of money exchange, a SIM card, snacks and gifts all at once.
It has six halls plus an IMAX theater. SM Cinema announced that the mall's IMAX theater reopened with IMAX with Laser in May 2026. Check the SM Cinema website for films and showtimes.

blocks.title: Outdoor dining at the fountain court

children.text: The fountain court behind the mall is lined with restaurants with outdoor terraces. After sunset it is less hot than midday, so it is a popular spot for dinner. Tenants change often, so check on site.
There is a semi-transparent indoor LED screen about

tall that debuted in August 2025. Wikipedia calls it the largest on Mindanao, but we could not confirm this from another source, so treat it as a decoration you may come across in the mall rather than something to plan around.

With a department store and a large supermarket, you can buy daily necessities, Filipino snacks and coffee, and food gifts at fairly stable prices. It is handy for picking out souvenirs on your last day.
The mall has a bowling center and the SMX Convention Center, making it a good place to spend time indoors with children on a rainy day. Check usage hours and fees on site.

blocks.title: Indoor rest from heat and rain

children.text: Davao is hot all year with frequent showers, so air-conditioned indoor space plays a big role in an itinerary. A cafe is a good place to plan your day or rest while charging your phone.
Arrive at the mall and check the floor layout on the map at the information desk. First cool off with a cold drink at a cafe.
Browse SM Store, the fashion shops and the bookstore at a relaxed pace and buy what you need.
At SM Supermarket, pick out food gifts such as snacks, coffee and Davao specialties.
Have dinner at the fountain-court restaurants behind the mall. When the weather is good, the outdoor seats are pleasantly cool.
If you want to see a movie, check the showtimes and book in advance. After the film, return to your hotel by Grab or taxi.

items.title: Airport-linked course
items.subtitle: A short visit on arrival or departure day

children.text: When the mall opens, leave your luggage at the hotel and head over by taxi or Grab. If it is before check-in, have a combined breakfast and lunch at the mall.
Have lunch in the dining area and buy things you need, such as a charger, medicine or snacks.
Use any spare time to relax at the cinema or a cafe. If you are departing, work backward from your airport arrival time to decide when to leave the mall.
The airport is a short taxi ride away, but leave with plenty of time to allow for rush-hour traffic.
Do not be complacent just because the airport is close; follow your airline's advice to arrive 2–3 hours before departure on both domestic and international flights.
From Manila (NAIA) to Davao International Airport (DVO), Cebu Pacific, Philippine Airlines (PAL) and others fly direct, and the flight takes about
2 hours
. The number of flights and fares change a lot with the season, so check when you book.
Davao International Airport is close to the Lanang district, so the trip to the mall is short.

items.title: From the airport to the mall

children.text: The mall is about
2.5km
in a straight line from the airport, and you go by taxi or Grab. Fares vary with the time of day and traffic, so ask the driver to turn on the meter.
Tell the driver "SM Lanang" or "SM Lanang Premier" and most will understand. It helps to name the exact drop-off point (main entrance, near the cinemas and so on).

According to Wikipedia, city bus routes toward Sasa, Panacan, Tibungco, Buhangin and Lasang pass the mall, and Davao BRT (bus rapid transit) routes also connect. Routes and stops can change, so confirm locally.
From the city center, taxi or Grab is the easiest. Asking the hotel front desk to call one is another option.
It is an indoor mall, so the seasons hardly matter. Its real value is as a place to escape the midday heat or sudden showers.

Crowding varies by time of day. Weekday mornings and early afternoons are relatively quiet, while weekend evenings and the December year-end season are busy. On its opening day so many visitors came that nearby roads jammed, so traffic can be heavy on weekends and event days.

Near the airport and the mall, the Lanang district has a cluster of mid-range and better hotels and serviced residences, which suits families and business travelers. Room rates vary a great deal with season and exchange rate, so check by date on a booking site. Getting to People's Park or the Roxas night market in the city center takes a ride, so choose your lodging to fit your route.

You can easily cover your meals inside the mall. It has Japanese, Korean and fast food, coffee chains and Filipino home cooking, and the fountain-court side has a dining area with outdoor seating. Tenants change often, so if you are after a specific restaurant, check the floor and opening status in the official SM Supermalls store directory. Cards are accepted at most places, but small shops may take cash only, so carry a little cash.

Korean travelers living locally often head out early for sightseeing in the city or to Samal Island or Mount Apo, then come back to the mall in the afternoon for a meal and shopping around showering and changing. If you do this, it helps to plan your ride back in advance to match the evening hours when the mall is open. For a large group, you can also book a van through your hotel instead of Grab, so agree and confirm the fare beforehand.
Official hours are
to
Monday to Thursday and Sunday, and
to
on Friday and Saturday. Some listings show different hours and they are extended at year end, so check the official channels.
In map apps, search both "SM Lanang" and "SM Lanang Premier". Either one leads to the same mall.
It is strongly air-conditioned inside, so bring a thin jacket.
There are bag checks at the entrance, so follow the staff's directions.
Check showtimes on the SM Cinema site or app and book popular films in advance. IMAX seats fill up quickly.
When calling Grab or a taxi, specify the exact pick-up and drop-off point, and leave extra time at rush hour because J.P. Laurel Avenue gets congested.
If you stop by before departing, leave your luggage at the hotel or a storage point and travel light.
At SM Supermarket, compare food gifts such as durian candy or Davao coffee.
The mall is big and easy to get lost in, so photograph the floor directory when you first arrive. Agree on a meeting place (the fountain court or the main entrance) in case your group gets separated.
Expansion plans for the mall have been reported, so some areas may be behind hoarding depending on when you visit. Check the latest notice before you go.
In crowded places, watch out for pickpockets and lost phones.
Opening hours, cinema operations and the tenant list change often. Check right before you visit.
Ask the taxi driver to turn on the meter, and consider Grab if you have a lot of luggage.
In an emergency or earthquake, follow staff directions and the emergency exit signs.
The SM Science Discovery Center inside the mall is reported to have been closed since 2015, so do not put it on your itinerary.
The Lanang district is in the north of Davao City, and the city center is about
20–30 minutes
away by taxi. It varies with the time of day and traffic.
This is the best-known church in central Davao. It is an easy trip from the mall by taxi or Grab.
An island just off Davao. It is best planned as a separate full-day trip rather than combined with mall shopping.
It is about
2.5km
from the mall, so it is easy to stop by briefly before departure.
